title.narrative: People-Centred Justice for Micro, Small, and Medium- sized Enterprises (mSMEs) and the People Behind Them

description.narrative: This programme aims to improve stability by reducing disputes within and betweenmSMEs affecting the livelihoods of the people behind them and increasing the formality ofthe sector by improving access to procedures. We will do this by collecting quality, detaileddata about the justice needs of small-business owners and their employees (justice needs andsatisfaction survey ‘JNS’), consolidating best practices for justice practitioners andsmall-business owners to more effectively address justice needs (guidelines), bringing togetherstakeholders to design innovative solutions to justice needs of small businesses (justiceinnovation labs ‘JIL’) and supporting nascent initiatives already addressing the justice needslocally (justice accelerator). For innovation to succeed, it needs an enabling environment:stakeholders need to understand the justice needs of mSMEs (through policy advice) and alignon political solutions.

This document presents a summary of the activities implemented by HiiL between November 2024 and October 2025 within the framework of the programme "People-Centred Justice for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (mSMEs) and the People Behind Them", funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Tunisia. We are pleased to share this first year of progress toward making justice systems work better for the entrepreneurs, family businesses, and workers who form the backbone of Tunisia’s economy. Together with our Tunisian partners, we have invested in strong evidence, collaborative design, and practical innovation, laying the foundations for justice services that prevent disputes, reduce informality, and unlock growth for the people behind mSMEs.

title.narrative: Enhanced access to data and knowledge about Justice Needs of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (mSMEs)

description.narrative: This Output relates to Outcome 1 (Access to Justice) in the Theory of Change and is crucial for evidence-based planning and data-driven service design by justice sector stakeholders. The data gathered informs all subsequent programme activities.

title.narrative: Number of perception studies and justice needs surveys conducted with NL support

comment.narrative: Soft copies of Justice Needs and Satisfaction surveys (JNS) published on HiiL website.

One justice needs survey published: 'Justice Needs and Satisfaction of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in Tunisia 2025: Legal problems in the informal and the formal sectors of the economy' (2,000 mSMEs interviewed). Report was published in English and Arabic.

title.narrative: Strengthened Dialogue and Policy Alignment on an Enabling Environment for mSME Justice

description.narrative: This Output relates to Outcome 2 (A People-centred Justice Sector) in the Theory of Change and is crucial for creating the enabling environment necessary for justice innovations to succeed and scale. The progress tracked involves advancing concrete initiatives like the co-development partnership with key public institutions to integrate solutions that simplify procedures for mSMEs, addressing the problem of informality.

title.narrative: Number of inclusive law and policy reform initiatives advanced.

comment.narrative: Official launch documents, MoUs, government decrees, and HiiL’s final strategy reports (e.g., Justice Transformation Strategy documents) confirming public commitment to the initiative.

The indicator tracks initiatives advanced during the reporting period that align with policy and institutional reform. The key reform initiative advanced is the establishment of a formal partnership with the RNE via an MoU to co-design and integrate an innovative solution from the Justice Innovation Lab (JIL) into RNE operations by 2026. This focuses on improving access to procedures like business registration for mSMEs. The initial Stakeholder Dialogue also served to align key actors across government and the business ecosystem to spotlight challenges and explore strategies for a more enabling business environment for mSMEs.

title.narrative: Strengthened dialogue and institutional capacity for mSME Justice

description.narrative: This Output relates to Outcome 2 (A People-centred Justice Sector) in the Theory of Change and is crucial for embedding new solutions and best practices within formal justice and regulatory bodies. Tracking this demonstrates that key institutions are adopting a more people-centred approach through co-creation and planned integration of innovative services.

title.narrative: Number of (formal/informal) justice institutions strengthened in terms of fairness, effectiveness, accountability or independence.

comment.narrative: The Means of Verification consists of HiiL's final institutional adoption measurement report (scheduled for 2025), complemented by co-created implementation plans and institutional records showing the integration of guidelines into training or practice.

1. National Business Registry (RNE): Formalized a partnership (MoU) and actively engaged in the Hack4Justice event and Justice Innovation Lab (JIL). The RNE is planning to integrate winning solutions (AI chatbot, company name generator prototype) into its systems and is positioned to integrate the JIL solution into its operations after piloting in 2026. This demonstrates advancement toward strengthening the institution's effectiveness and accountability through digital transformation. 2. National Bar Association: Engaged with new leadership to solidify an ongoing partnership and make arrangements for capacity-building for young lawyers in 2026. This lays the groundwork for strengthening the effectiveness of legal practitioners in supporting mSMEs

title.narrative: Increased Access to Justice for owners and people working in mSMEs

description.narrative: This indicator measures the Impact achieved through the delivery of new and scaled-up justice services (resolution only). It directly tracks progress toward Outcome 1 (Access to Justice) in the Theory of Change, representing the total number of people using the services created by the programme.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries (f/m) with access to justice

comment.narrative: This target represents the projected total reach of new and scaled-up justice services across resolution pathways (Startups, Guidelines, JIL). The figure incorporates the anticipated initial usage of resolution services from the Guidelines (3,600 users) and the projected volume of users for the startups in the Venture Growth Hub (960). As the programme is designed for scalability, these resolution and prevention services are expected to reach their full operational scale to begin closing the justice gap primarily after the programme’s conclusion.

The achievement of this outcome was delayed because Year 1 focused on data collection (JNS) and service co-creation (JIL/Guidelines), which are prerequisites. The JIL pilot begins in Year 2, and formal training for practitioners on the Guidelines begins in Q1 2026, which is when the uptake of services (Actual) will begin to register against the target.
